attrs.evidence: NOT ESTABLISHED, and the falsifiers are shipped so that it cannot be assumed. scripts/check-derivation.mjs --falsifiers builds three registries that satisfy FAC-DERIVATION-ACYCLIC completely and fail to reproduce: a clock-dependent command, an RNG-dependent command, and a command whose real input is an undeclared environment variable. Each is admitted by the graph check and each produces different bytes or different output on a second run. The artifact's own derived products are re-run and compared by scripts/verify-review-artifact.mjs, which is a weaker and honest empirical fact: they reproduced on this machine, under this toolchain, at this moment.
attrs.gap: EVERY CLAUSE IS UNDONE. Nothing declares a material-input set beyond the argv; the toolchain is recorded as a provenance string in the receipt and is not pinned or verified; environment is scrubbed with `env -i` at verification time and is not declared per product; no product declares a nondeterminism policy. The re-derivation check in verify-review-artifact.mjs would pass a product that is reproducible only because nobody changed the machine.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6 adjudication §7, rejecting Fable's PROOFS.md P3 as stated. SLSA build levels and reproducible-builds practice treat hermeticity and reproducibility as requirements distinct from build-graph shape.
attrs.review_focus: The falsifiers prove acyclicity is insufficient. What is the smallest declaration that would make one real product in this registry hermetic enough to carry evidential force — and is that even the right target, or should derived products be typed as non-hermetic evidence and consumed accordingly?
attrs.statement: A derived product carries reproducible evidential force only when all material inputs are declared and content-bound, the transitive toolchain and runtime are pinned, environment inputs are declared or neutralised, network and mutable references are blocked or recorded under an explicit non-hermetic evidence type, and nondeterminism is eliminated, seeded, normalised or explicitly modelled.
